direction: The alert tells the customer what was seen, what the bank has done, what to do now and how to check the message is real, and says nothing about why it was flagged.
dont_over_correct: Do not put the full card number, account number or balance in the text. Do not add a link to "see details". Do not send long explanations. Keep to the fields above; if the fraud team does not approve a field, leave it out and say where to find it.
prompt: Every fraud alert states the transaction (as approved), what was done to the card or account, one answerable question and how to verify the message, and never why it was flagged.
design: Name the transaction as the customer would recognize it.
Say what the bank has done.
Ask one question the customer can answer.
Give a route that does not need a call.
Say how to verify the message.
Say what happens if there is no reply.
If a detail is unavailable, say so.
setup_questions: Can your agent supply these fields: alert.transaction_fields, alert.action_taken, alert.channel, customer.reply_options?
Where does the fix go in your agent: the system prompt?

evals.behaviour: Fields in the first message: Name the transaction as the customer would recognize it
evals.pass_if: The alert shows the card last four, the amount, the merchant, the time, and the channel.

evals.behaviour: Do nothing special: keep it short and approved: Don't over-correct
evals.pass_if: A short confirmation that the card is unpaused and the alert is closed. No full card number, no balance, no link.
evals.fail_if: Full card number, balance, or a "see details" link added

guardrail.condition: a fraud or unusual-activity alert is about to be sent, and the reply breaks the rule: every fraud alert states the transaction (as approved), what was done to the card or account, one answerable question and how to verify the message, and never why it was flagged.
